name: AI, authorship and the future of the literary - A conversation about creativity, consciousness, authorship and the future of books.
description:
A poem in seconds. A story at the click of a button. Research, rewriting, imitation, ideas on demand.
If a machine can now do so much of what we associate with writing, what exactly are writers doing?
And what happens to the things that cannot be reduced to a prompt: the particularity of a place, the accumulation of experience, the strange things that catch our attention, the forms we fall in love with, the discoveries we make while trying to write?
AI, authorship and the future of the literary brings together celebrated Writer, poet and essayist Anjum Hasan, literary and cultural studies scholar Elizabeth Thomas, and Ravi Chakraborty, Programme Director of Alliance University's MA Creative Writing programme, for a lively roundtable on writing in the age of AI.
The conversation will move across fiction, poetry, nonfiction, screenwriting and other forms of storytelling, asking what changes when AI enters the picture. We will talk about literary consciousness and imitation, originality and authorship, research and discovery, and the choices writers make before, during and after putting words on the page. We will also look at what AI means for publishing: for writers, editors, publishers and readers, and for the idea of the book as something made through many kinds of human labour.
For a programme that teaches people to write, AI also presents a more immediate question: what should we be teaching writers now? What kinds of attention and experimentation become more important when machines can generate language so easily? Can close observation of one's environment, encounters with other forms and sustained experimentation become ways of developing a voice that cannot simply be prompted into existence?
And perhaps the most interesting question is not whether AI will replace writers, but what we might discover about writing by being forced to ask what only writing, and writers, can do.
The roundtable will be genuinely open, with questions and interventions from the audience woven into the conversation.
At Atta Galatta, a space built around the physical book, the conversation will also touch on the curious fact that a book is never just words: it is a work shaped by writers, editors, designers, publishers and readers, and by the many human decisions that bring it into the world.
Come with your questions. Your doubts about AI. Your enthusiasms. Your arguments about what counts as writing.

Listeners Circle is an initiative to facilitate listening without judgment, hence giving a safe space for anyone to speak their heart out without the fear of judgment. name: Human Library  - Meetup
description:
Each chapter of Human Library is a guided space for meaningful, non-judgmental conversations, structured by thoughtful prompts. These prompts allow attendees to explore different perspectives, stories, and memories.

You can choose to listen to others' stories and share your own when you feel comfortable. Every participant takes turns sharing a memory, opinion, or experience related to the prompt assigned to them.

Note: This is not a dating event.

Structure of the event:

1. Introduction of attendees and the host.
2. Attendees are divided into smaller groups.
3. Each group receives a bowl of prompts.
3. Prompts are divided into three levels: Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3.
4. Level 1 prompts help people get to know each other.
Example: What is your earliest childhood memory?
5. Level 2 prompts encourage deeper conversations.
Example: What is one habit from your lifestyle that you would recommend to others?
6. Once Level 1 and Level 2 conversations are completed, the smaller groups are merged for Level 3 prompts.
7. Depending on the number of attendees, either one or two larger groups are formed for Level 3 conversations
Age Group- 18+

name: The Haunting of Kunjamma P. - Book launch
description:
Join us for the book launch of “The Haunting of Kunjamma P.” by Shinie Antony, hosted in conversation with theatre artist and facilitator Jimmy Xavier. Together, they will explore the story behind the book, Shinie’s journey as an author, and the themes of satire and social criticism that shape her latest work.
The Haunting of Kunjamma P. is a darkly funny novel set in rural Kerala about a hyper-religious woman who gets possessed by a  literary demon. Published by Hachette India, it is described by writer Benyamin as 'a novel that combines life, satire and social criticism in a way never seen before'.
Shinie Antony has written the novellas Eden Abandoned: The Story of Lilith (Laadli Fiction Award 2025, Wise Owl Literary Award for Fiction 2025, Ruskin Bond Award for Fiction 2026), Can’t (longlist 2024 Crossword Book Awards), and The Girl Who Couldn’t Love. Also, short-story collections Barefoot and Pregnant, The Orphanage for Words; and compiled anthologies Hell Hath No Fury, Boo, Why We Don’t Talk, An Unsuitable Woman, and co-edited The Art of Holding On, Letting Go. Her story A Dog’s Death won the Commonwealth Short Story Asia prize in 2002. She is the Founder of the Bangalore Literature Festival and Director of the Bengaluru Poetry Festival. The Haunting of Kunjamma P is her latest novel. 
 
Jimmy Xavier is a true-blue Bangalorean boy, with close to 27 years of experience in theatre and 23 in radio. With about 1500 theatre shows, his work connects him to some of the best theatre collectives in Bangalore, from roles ranging from the absurd to the very dramatic. He, along with his partner, run the theatre group Jugaad Co. He has designed and conducted multiple theatre training workshops in schools, colleges and corporates. He also consults with Training Sideways as a facilitator and content creator where he uses theatre, storytelling and games to create training modules for corporates. He currently hosts a podcast on Bangalore -- 'Jimmy Jimmy the Show' -- on YouTube and Instagram. He used to host the morning show on Radio Mirchi in Bangalore.

name: Zine & Tell - Art Workshop
description:
Zine & Tell is a fun, hands-on afternoon of making, exploring and getting a little creative. A zine is a small, self-published magazine that can be about absolutely anything — your interests, thoughts, stories, favourite things, random obsessions or little pieces of your world.
We’ll take a quick look at where zines came from and how people have used them as a way to express themselves, share ideas and tell stories outside the usual rules of publishing. Then, you’ll get to create your very own zine, bringing together all the things that make you — through writing, doodling, cutting, pasting, illustrating and a little bit of everything in between.
There’s no right way to make a zine and definitely no artistic skills required. Just come with an open mind, explore your creativity, meet some new people and maybe leave with a few new friends (and your very own little magazine!)

name: Brush Pen Calligraphy Workshop - Calligraphy Workshop
description:
Ever wanted to try calligraphy but didn’t know where to begin.
Join us for a calm, colourful and hands-on brush pen calligraphy experience where you’ll learn everything from the very basics and gradually build your way towards creating your own piece of artwork.
Whether you’ve never held a brush pen before or simply want to explore calligraphy in a relaxed setting, no prior experience is required. We’ll take it step by step, with plenty of guidance along the way.
All you need to do is show up, slow down, and enjoy creating. ♡
What to expect
✦ Start from the basics — understand the brush pen, strokes, pressure and letter formation.
✦ Learn step by step — practise at your own pace with guided exercises and worksheets.
✦ Create with high-quality materials — all the materials you need for the workshop are provided, including your calligraphy kit.
✦ Make your own take-home piece — put everything you’ve learnt together and create something you can take home with you.
✦ Post-workshop guidance — have questions after the workshop or want to continue practising? You can reach out to me for guidance related to your calligraphy journey.
Meet your instructor
Jerrlin Shiny — Calligraphy Instructor & Artist
With a Diploma in Calligraphy and 6 years of experience teaching calligraphy, Jerrlin’s approach is centred around making the learning process approachable, enjoyable and pressure-free.

name: Kartik in Cosmic Chaos - Book Signing
description:
Join us for the book signing of Kartik in Cosmic Chaos with the author Jigyasa.
About the book:
Kartik’s journey through space begins as an adventure but slowly becomes a quiet challenge to everything he believes about intelligence, emotion, and life. As he encounters alien worlds and unfamiliar minds, he is forced to rethink his deeply human way of seeing the universe.
Guided by curiosity as much as confusion, Kartik moves through strange planets, unexpected friendships, and encounters that are at once funny, unsettling, and deeply humane. Science runs through the stories like a living thread, shaping a future that feels imaginative yet strangely possible.
Witty, warm, and thought-provoking, these futuristic short stories invite readers to laugh, wonder, and question what it truly means to understand another being—even one that is alien. Written for readers aged 12 and above.
About the author:
Jigyasa studied Neuroscience at the University of Massachusetts, Amherst, before finding her way into science writing—and eventually fiction. A freelance science writer for over a decade, she blends scientific insight with imagination. Her literary work has appeared in The Hindu and the literary magazine Muse India.

name: Public Disappearances - Book launch
description:
Join us on Saturday, October 31, 2026, at 11 AM for an intimate literary morning celebrating the launch of Public Disappearances: Saunters and Sojourns in Europe by the acclaimed poet Debasish Lahiri.
Conceived in the utter solitude of worldly ruminations, this evocative poetry collection offers a profound exploration of place, memory, and the common incongruities of human experience. Written during extended periods of living across several European nations, the poems capture a distinct perspective that shifts seamlessly between the intimate gaze of the insider and the detached observation of the outsider.
Whether wandering through bustling historic streets or pausing in quiet, forgotten corners, the evening will immerse you in the quiet saunters and reflective sojourns that shaped this deeply moving work.
The discussions will also look at the role of European art in the shaping of the poetry, bringing into purview his ekphrastic book A Certain Penance of Light as well.

name: Breaking the News - Media Literacy Workshop
description:
News finds us everywhere: on Instagram, WhatsApp, television, articles, newspapers, and even opinion reels.
Today, children are growing up in a digital world where information comes at them from every direction, with misinformation, disinformation, and AI-altered content increasingly woven into what they consume. Because of this, it becomes an essential skill to make sense of it, recognize different perspectives, and decide what deserves our trust.
Breaking the News helps children look beyond the headlines and understand how the news they consume is created and shaped.
Our Method:
Children step into the shoes of reporters and investigate a news event through fun roleplay and interactive challenges. They uncover different perspectives and explore their choices about what to include, leave out, and how that can shape the public narrative.
What They Will Leave With:
Children will:

Learn to recognise misinformation, propaganda, disinformation and AI-altered content.
Build the habit of questioning, comparing sources, and looking for evidence before forming an opinion.
Understand how media representation shapes what we see as important or unimportant.
Build curiosity about current affairs and the world around them.

Who Should Attend:
This workshop is ideal for parents who want their child to:

Learn to read and engage with news critically, not passively.
Build news and media literacy in an increasingly digital world.
Understand how different perspectives can shape the way we see an issue.
Develop the habit of questioning information, seeking evidence, and thinking for themselves.
Become more thoughtful and informed participants in the world around them.

name: KALIGHAT PAINTINGS - WHERE TRADITION MEETS MODERNITY
description:
Step into the vibrant world of Kalighat Painting, one of Bengal's most distinctive folk-art traditions, in an immersive workshop.
This workshop goes beyond simply creating a painting. It is an opportunity to discover the story, culture, history, and visual language behind Kalighat art and understand how this traditional art form evolved with changing times.
Beginning with the origins of Kalighat paintings in 19th-century Kolkata, the workshop explores the artistic community of Patuas, the influence of the Kalighat Temple, and the bustling world around it that shaped this unique art tradition.
Participants will discover how Kalighat artists moved from depicting Hindu deities and mythological stories to portraying everyday life, contemporary society, humour, and social observations. Through these works, the paintings became a fascinating visual record of Bengal's changing social landscape.
A key part of the workshop will be understanding the distinctive Kalighat visual language—its confident flowing lines, bold contours, expressive figures, simplified forms, and vibrant compositions. We will also explore how Bengal's folk traditions influenced modern Indian art, particularly through the work of Jamini Roy.
The session combines storytelling, art appreciation, visual references, demonstrations, and hands-on practice, allowing participants to first understand the tradition and then interpret it through their own artwork.
Participants will be guided through the process of creating a Kalighat-inspired painting, making the experience both educational and creative. No prior art experience is required—just curiosity and a willingness to explore.
WHAT YOU WILL EXPERIENCE

The fascinating history and evolution of Kalighat Painting
Stories behind its mythological, social, and everyday-life themes
An exploration of the Patuas and the Kalighat tradition
The influence of Jamini Roy and Bengal's folk-art vocabulary
Understanding of lines, forms, colours, composition, and expression
A guided hands-on Kalighat-inspired painting session
Your own completed artwork to take home

Through Hues by Sindhoor, this workshop aims to make traditional Indian art experiential rather than simply instructional—giving participants the opportunity to connect with a living artistic tradition through its stories, forms, and their own creative expression.
Come discover Kalighat—not just as a style of painting, but as a window into Bengal's history, culture, people, and imagination.

name: Authentic Relating Games  - Playful yet deep games to help people connect
description:
Ever wonder what is possible when we drop the small talk and connect for real?

Authentic Relating Games is a global practice of guided, playful yet deep exercises (the 'games') designed to help people connect more honestly and meaningfully — whether with close friends or complete strangers.

Through structured partner and group conversations, you will get to practice speaking from the heart, deep listening, and noticing what's alive in you as you relate to others.  The games create space for more honesty, curiosity, and real human connection — often in ways that feel surprisingly fun, refreshing, and profoundly moving.

What to Expect

- A Structured Container:  We will start as a full group to set some simple guidelines that ensure the space feels safe, respectful, and confidential.
- Activities with Partners, Trios, and the Large Group: We'll keep changing partners throughout the session (no need to bring a partner!).
- Guided Prompts and Demos: We'll guide you step-by-step through the games and provide live demonstrations so you know what to do.
- Total Autonomy: You are always in the driver's seat.  You choose how deeply you want to go, or pass on a prompt or game at any time.
- A New Set of Games: If you attended Authentic Relating Games previously, don't worry this won't be the same games but a different set of activities to explore!

No experience needed.  Come as you are.  If you've never done anything like this before, don't worry — it's simple and there is no pressure to get it "right".

About the facilitator:
Roy Jacob is the founder of the Conscious Communication Academy and has been facilitating workshops and retreats for over 15 years, mostly for changemakers as well as team retreats for NGOs and companies.  Roy grew up in the U.S. before finding his calling and coming to India (where his roots are) in 2003.  He believes in the transformative power of combining radical honesty with radical care.
